title: Miranda v. Arizona (1966)
key_points: Holding: Before custodial interrogation, a suspect must be warned of the right to remain silent, that statements can be used against them, and the right to an attorney (appointed if needed).
officer_notes: Scenario: You arrest a burglary suspect and, in the patrol car, ask him where the stolen items are.
Takeaway: Custody plus questioning means warnings first.
